provenance_note: Every reference value is re-derived in the corpus from SPEC-iolist and the cited standards by an author without access to this page; this run recomputes every check from the shipping build through window.__iolistEvaluate, and no stored result of this tool is reused.
reference: Independent reference corpus for the I/O List tool (iolist.html). It covers the signal-list checks, the ISA-5.1 letter-code parse of spec 4.2, the NAMUR NE 43 current levels of spec 4.3, the card-count and placement arithmetic of spec 4.4-4.6, the counts and spare fractions of spec 4.7, all 37 review rules IOL-R-001...037 with a triggering case and a near-miss each, the stated boundary behaviour (spare fraction exactly at target, a limit at a range end and at hi+2*eps, racks equal to racks required, a six-letter candidate run, channels 256 versus 257, spare target 0.9), the verdict and package_savable logic of spec 6, and the four presets of spec 9 with the expected values the specification prints for them. Sources: SPEC-iolist.md (spec date 2026-09-22), ANSI/ISA-5.1-2022 identification letters as the spec transcribes them, NAMUR NE 43 signal levels (3.8-20.5 mA measurement, <=3.6 or >=21 mA failure, verified against Lesman Instrument Co.'s reproduction), and IEC 61131-2:2017 Ed. 4.0 clause structure 6.4/6.5 for the digital and analog I/O families (verified against the publicly posted table of contents). All arithmetic references were computed with the stdlib script iolist-ref.py beside this file, which re-implements spec 4.1-4.7, 5 and 6 and asserts every hand-written expectation below before the corpus is written.
reference_citations: SPEC-iolist.md, spec date 2026-09-22 (_docs/SPEC-iolist.md), sections 3-7, 9, 13-15: the normative data model, formulas, rules and preset expectations.

ANSI/ISA-5.1-2022 Instrumentation Symbols and Identification, clause 4, Table 4.1 identification letters, as transcribed in SPEC-iolist.md basis label [ISA]; the first letters used here (A analysis, F flow, H hand, L level, P pressure, S speed/frequency, T temperature, X unclassified, Y event/state/presence, Z position/dimension) were cross-checked against a public ISA-5.1 first-letter reference. The corpus author did not read a licensed copy of the 2022 text; the letters the spec marks [ISA-conv] (succeeding E, A, L; modifiers M, C, F, Q) are author method.

NAMUR NE 43 Standardization of the Signal Level for the Failure Information of Digital Transmitters: measurement information 3.8 ... 20.5 mA, failure information <= 3.6 mA or >= 21 mA. Verified against Lesman Instrument Co., 'What does NAMUR NE 43 do for me?' (https://www.lesman.com/what-does-namur-ne-43-do-for-me), which states the 3.8-20.5 mA measurement range and the <=3.6 / >=21 mA failure levels. The 2021 edition's control-system detection margin was not read and is not used (spec 2 limitation 5).

IEC 61131-2:2017 Ed. 4.0 (2017-08), Programmable controllers - Part 2: Equipment requirements and tests, clause 6.4 Digital I/Os (6.4.4 digital inputs current sinking, 6.4.5 digital outputs for alternating currents, 6.4.6 digital outputs for direct current) and clause 6.5 Analog I/Os (6.5.2 analog inputs, 6.5.3 analog outputs, 6.5.4 analog temperature inputs). Clause titles and the 2017-08 edition date verified against the publicly posted preview of the standard's table of contents at plcopen.org. No numeric limit from the standard is used; the electrical-type vocabulary of spec 3.4 is author method built on these clause families.
tolerance: Categorical outputs are exact: verdict, package_savable, the finding map (rule@target -> severity), per-rule finding counts, severity counts, letter-code parses with their expected sets, address strings, the sorted unallocated list, and every integer count (n, c, V, C_req, C, channels, allocated, spare, cards, racks_required, counts by controller and signal type). spare_frac is compared to absolute 1e-12: it is the ratio of two integers computed by one division, so the only error is the final rounding. NE 43 values are compared to relative 1e-9 with an absolute floor of 1e-9*span, the tolerance spec 13 states, because x(I) = lo + (I - 0.004)/0.016*span is one affine map with a single division and no iteration. No tolerance here was widened to let a value pass; each follows from the arithmetic of the quantity it covers. Checks marked "disputable": true rest on a reading of the specification that another reading could change; the reason is stated in the check's derivation. The adapter reads those sentences as: exact deep equality; spare_frac to absolute 1e-12 and every other group or controller field exact; NE 43 levels to relative 1e-9 with an absolute floor of 1e-9*span, span taken from the reference as (x_sat_hi - x_sat_lo)/1.04375. A letter `expected` list is compared as the set SPEC 4.2 defines, so both sides are sorted.

ambiguities: RESOLVED by adjudication 2026-09-23: spec 13 now defines unallocated[] as every point with signal_type other than FB that carries no channel address, and the spec 5 evaluation note was rewritten to say that 'excluded from allocation' excludes an IOL-R-018/019 row from the group arithmetic of spec 4.4 only. Cases r018-unknown-controller, r019-sil-on-bpcs and unallocated-every-addressless-channel-point rest on that definition and are no longer disputable.

Spec 6 lists `empty` above `blocked`. A state with no points and an invalid hardware definition therefore returns `empty` here; a reading that gives blockers precedence would return `blocked` (case r017-empty-points-verdict-empty, marked disputable).

RESOLVED by adjudication 2026-09-23 against the corpus: spec 13 now states that an IOL-R-017 hardware path always ends in a field, so a duplicate `installed` entry points at installed[i].card_type_id. Case r017-installed-duplicate-pair was corrected from installed[1].

RESOLVED by adjudication 2026-09-23: spec 13 now names the voted entry's `from` id as the IOL-R-036 target. Cases r036-voted-group-mismatch and r036-two-entries-same-tags rest on it and are no longer disputable.

IOL-R-023 is raised 'one finding per (voting group, card)' while spec 13 gives the target as the voting group name, so two breaching cards in one group collapse to one entry in a rule@target map. Case r023-two-cards-two-findings (added by adjudication) tests the pair through findings_by_rule; the target string still cannot tell the two cards apart and the specification still does not say it should.

Spec 3.1 caps settings.default_spare at [0, 0.9] and spec 5 IOL-R-017 raises a blocker outside it, but the spec does not say what value the computation then uses. The corpus falls back to the spec 3.1 default 0.2 (case r017-default-spare-negative, marked disputable).

Spec 4.6 orders a controller's cards by 'position of ct in k.card_type_ids', which is undefined for a group created only by an `installed` entry naming a card type the controller does not list. No case here relies on that order.
Spec 5 IOL-R-018 asks only whether a controller with the row's id exists, so a controller that is itself invalid under IOL-R-017 still counts as present. No case here turns on that.

Spec 4.3 defines the NE 43 levels 'For AI with electrical_type in {ma420, ma420_hart}', so a 4-20 mA analog output gets no NE 43 row even though the same current levels apply to it physically (case ne43-not-computed).

Spec 5 evaluates IOL-R-033 as |l.value - hi| <= eps(p) and IOL-R-031 as l.value > hi + eps(p). In exact arithmetic these meet without a gap, but in binary floating point a value at exactly hi + eps can fail both tests: with lo = 0 and hi = 1e6 Pa, (1e6 + 1e-3) - 1e6 evaluates above 1e-9*1e6 while 1e6 + 1e-3 is not above 1e6 + 1e-9*1e6. The corpus keeps its boundary cases at hi, hi + eps/2 and hi + 2*eps so no check rests on that gap.

Spec 5 IOL-R-022 reads k.racks directly, while spec 5 IOL-R-017 declares racks = 0 a hardware-definition blocker. The corpus lets both fire on the same state (case r017-racks-zero, marked disputable); a reading in which an invalid field is not read would raise IOL-R-017 alone.

Spec 13 defines letter[tag_key] as {code, f, expected[]} or null but does not say what `expected` holds when f is unclassified. The corpus uses null for `expected` and null for `f` when R is empty (cases r005-no-succeeding-letter, parse-candidate-examples).

Spec 3.3.1 makes a second `installed` entry for one (controller, card type) pair an error but does not say which of the two entries sets C. The corpus and the tool both use the first (case r017-installed-duplicate-pair, groups check still marked disputable); adjudication 2026-09-23 left this open because no benchmark check turns on it.

Spec 4.7 reports a line per controller and spec 4.4 a group per (controller, card type), and neither says whether a controller that IOL-R-017 declares invalid is still reported. Case r017-empty-controller-id (added by adjudication, second pass) therefore checks the findings, the verdict, the unallocated list, the unassigned counts column and the address map, and not groups or controllers.
